video.title: The Easiest $3K/Day Business Nobody Is Talking About

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Sariah (27, Utah), who started Memory Magnets Co with under $1,000 in 2024 after her husband's low pay and second job left the family broke. She sells custom photo magnets online, at markets and as an on-the-spot wedding/event service, and sells magnet-making machine kits plus refill supplies and courses. She claims $1.63M online revenue in her first full year (about $600K profit), a $233K best month and a $100.5K first six-figure month after six months. Key takeaway: a simple, high-margin physical product plus a service at price-insensitive events (weddings), marketed through short-form video, grew fast, and teaching others to copy the model became a second revenue line.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office podcast

speakers.name: Sariah
speakers.description: Founder of Memory Magnets Co (memorymagnetsco.com), Utah, age 27

ideas.name: Custom photo magnet shop (online and markets)
ideas.one_liner: Print customers' photos as fridge magnets, sold online via Shopify and at local markets.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales (packs of magnets), repeat buyers
ideas.customer: Consumers who want to display photos without frames, such as families, new couples and moms
ideas.problem: People take thousands of photos and never look at them; they want to display memories without covering walls in frames.
ideas.offer: Custom printed photo magnets, e.g. a nine-pack for $25, made from customer-uploaded photos.

pricing.notes: Smallest magnets have about 91% margin; materials about 35 cents per magnet.

acquisition_channels.details: In-person local markets (booth fees $50-$300); handing out business cards; customers return or order online for about five days after a market from that area.
Short-form videos mostly showing the magnets being made; consistency stressed; followers become repeat buyers.

quote.text: a lot of just showing us making the product is probably what we do most. I think people just like to see the process.
quote.speaker: Sariah

acquisition_channels.details: Repeat buyers from markets and weddings follow the social accounts and are reminded of the product.

ideas.delivery: Photos are printed on an Epson inkjet and pressed into magnets by hand by the owner and helpers (high school kids paid $12-15/hour); shipped for online orders.
unit_economics_claims: $1.63M online revenue last year with about 30-40% net margin overall
Best market over $3,000 revenue in a two-day market; worst about $150
First month profit a little over $1,000
ideas.startup_cost: Under $1,000, put on a credit card (machine and printer)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First month (May-June 2024) made a little over $1,000 profit; $10K month in about 2-3 months; $100K month in about 6 months

acquisition.how: Content and online store are inbound and can be agent-assisted; the markets that drove early growth are physical and human.

onboarding.how: Online ordering with upload tools is largely self-serve.

delivery.how: Physical printing, pressing and shipping require a person; mostly manual.

support.how: Order questions and photo issues can be handled by agents with human checks.

uk_applicability.notes: Photo magnets sell the same in the UK. UK markets and craft fairs exist, and Shopify and inkjet printing work the same. Prices and materials sourcing differ.

risks: Seasonality, with fewer markets in winter

ideas.name: On-the-spot magnet photo service at weddings and events
ideas.one_liner: Hire out a magnet-making station at weddings, parties and baby showers where guests get free magnets paid for by the host.
ideas.business_model: Per-event fee (flat or hourly plus bulk magnet rate)
ideas.customer: Engaged couples and event hosts (weddings, baby showers, graduations, corporate/military events)
ideas.problem: Hosts want a memorable, unique guest favor at a one-off event.
ideas.offer: A live magnet station: guests have photos taken or uploaded, magnets are printed and pressed on the spot and given free to guests.

pricing.model: Flat event fee or hourly rate plus bulk magnet rate; suggested per-head pricing
pricing.notes: Host suggested per-head pricing ($20-30 per guest) to simplify quotes. Sariah says the baby shower could have been $500.

acquisition_channels.details: Posted wedding videos on social media; couples emailed in with no outbound outreach.

quote.text: we haven't really done any outreach other than posting about it once or twice. Um, it really all comes from people coming to us about it.
quote.speaker: Sariah

acquisition_channels.details: First wedding came from customers at her second market who bought about 40 magnets and then asked her to do their wedding.
Wedding expos mentioned as a channel others have had success with.

ideas.delivery: Staff set up a backdrop, take or receive photos, print and press magnets on site. Currently needs about four people; a new QR-code upload software would cut it to 1-2.
unit_economics_claims: Recent $2,000 wedding: about 300 magnets (about $100 materials) plus gas, about $5
With labor at $25/hour for 3 people, costs ~$400 giving about an 80% margin (host's math)
tools: QR code photo upload software (in development)
ideas.startup_cost: Same machine and printer as the magnet shop; under $1,000 to start
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: First wedding came from her second market, within about the first few months

acquisition.how: Inbound via video content and referrals; wedding directories and expos could be added. All inbound.

onboarding.how: Quote and booking can be handled by forms and agents; custom details need checking.

delivery.how: Must be physically present at events to print and press.

billing.how: Deposits and invoices via online payment tools.

support.how: Pre-event questions by agent; on-the-day issues need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: UK weddings are also high-spend and price insensitive. Photo booth and wedding favor vendors are established in the UK. Travel and public liability insurance would be needed.

quotes.text: the couple basically pays pays us and then the magnets are free.
quotes.speaker: Sariah

quotes.text: We quoted them $2,000 and it was just me, my mom and dad, my husband
quotes.speaker: Sariah

ideas.name: Magnet machine starter kits and refill supplies
ideas.one_liner: Sell complete magnet-making machine kits to aspiring entrepreneurs, plus recurring supply refills.
ideas.business_model: One-off equipment sales plus consumables refills, with lifetime warranty
ideas.customer: Aspiring side-hustlers such as single moms, new moms, and jobless moms who want a home business
ideas.problem: Buying a machine from China is confusing and risky; buyers want support and a clear business-start path.
ideas.offer: Machine kits with support, a lifetime warranty, Shopify and live events courses, and refill supplies.

pricing.notes: Machine price not stated; margins about 30% on machines; little margin on refills.

acquisition_channels.details: Social content and sharing how to run the business; people reach out asking to start.
Customers of magnets and events who become aware of the kit business.

ideas.delivery: Ship machines and supplies; lifetime warranty (replace broken machines); community and course support.

delivery.how: Physical shipping and warranty replacement are manual or 3PL.

support.how: Heavy volume of questions, currently answered by the founder; could be partially agent-assisted.

uk_applicability.notes: UK buyers need UK-compatible machine, voltage and sourcing, consumer rights and warranty obligations. Otherwise the same.

quotes.text: we sell them the machine and then we also sell refill supplies. So anytime they need more supplies for magnets, they'll come back.
quotes.speaker: Sariah

ideas.name: Business-start course and QR upload software for magnet makers
ideas.one_liner: Courses (Shopify, live events, overall start-a-business) and a QR photo-upload app sold to magnet entrepreneurs.
ideas.customer: People wanting to start a magnet business
ideas.problem: Many people ask how to start (EIN, sales, growth) and she can't answer everyone.
ideas.offer: Courses covering every aspect of the business plus in-development software for customers to upload and crop photos by QR.

acquisition_channels.details: Existing customers and followers asking questions.

uk_applicability.notes: Course content references US items like EIN; UK equivalents would be needed.

quotes.text: we're working on just like an overall course that walks through literally every aspect we have gone through in this business
quotes.speaker: Sariah

ideas.name: New product lines on the same machines (restickable backing, pins, bottle openers)
ideas.one_liner: Expand the machine range to produce restickable backings, pins and bottle openers.
ideas.business_model: Product sales of machines and items
ideas.problem: Customers want variety; supplier risk is lowered by owning product lines.
ideas.offer: Restickable photo backings (up to 20 times), round machine for pins and bottle openers.

ideas.name: Wedding arch rental
ideas.one_liner: Build a wooden arch for about $200 and rent it repeatedly for $400-600.

quotes.text: they build or they built a wedding arch and they just rent out that arch for couples to get married under for like 400 bucks a wedding.

ideas.name: Wedding vendor add-ons (photo booth, gelato carts, cannoli carts, singing pizza guy)
ideas.one_liner: Other niche wedding rental and service ideas.
ideas.offer: Photo booth rentals, carts and novelty acts at weddings.

quotes.text: photo booth rentals at weddings or shakuderie carts at weddings or canoli cards or a pizza guy that sings Italian songs.

ideas.name: Appliance rentals via Facebook Marketplace
ideas.one_liner: Rent out washers and dryers for about $60/month via Facebook Marketplace listings.
ideas.customer: Renters and movers who don't want to buy a washer/dryer
ideas.problem: Buying appliances is costly and inconvenient for people who might move.
ideas.offer: Rent washer/dryer with delivery, insurance and repairs.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook Marketplace listings; customers found rentals while searching to buy.

ideas.delivery: Deliver and install; fix if broken.
unit_economics_claims: $60 a month rental price per customer

acquisition.how: Listings can be agent-managed, platform terms apply.

uk_applicability.notes: Appliance rental exists in the UK; Gumtree and Facebook Marketplace work.

tactics.name: Use markets to land first wedding customers
steps: Sign up for local markets (booth fees $50-$300; higher-fee markets usually have better traffic)
Hand out business cards because rushed shoppers order online within about five days
Film events and post on social so couples find you

quote.text: The ones that I pay $300 for are the ones that I make the most at
quote.speaker: Sariah

tactics.name: Price weddings per head or flat
steps: Charge flat or per-head (e.g. $20-30 per guest) instead of itemised hourly plus bulk
Bake in assumptions on magnets per guest to protect margin

quote.text: I always try to simplify pricing as much as possible
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Reduce labor with QR upload software
steps: Guests scan a QR code, upload and crop photos
Photos flow into a print template
One person prints and one presses; cut staff from four to one or two

quote.text: you really only need one person
quote.speaker: Sariah

tactics.name: Track QR codes on magnet backs
steps: Print a tracking-link QR code on 100 to 1,000 magnets
Use a URL shortener such as TinyURL for tracking
Review scans over a month before scaling

quote.text: I would do like a 100 or 1,000 magnet test.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Trust through warranty
steps: Provide community and course support so buyers prefer you over buying direct from China

quote.text: We have like a lifetime warranty on all of our kits.
quote.speaker: Sariah

tactics.name: Share openly to grow the market
steps: Become the expert and reach others who want to enter
Sell kits, courses and supplies to the audience

quote.text: I don't think it will ever be oversaturated.

warnings.warning: Cheap local customers and copycats can undermine pricing.
Don't assume a market is oversaturated based on listings alone.

lessons.lesson: Start with a small experiment: she began with under $1,000 after searching for a way to display photos.

quote.text: you just have to jump in and then you learn as you go.
quote.speaker: Sariah

lessons.lesson: Events like weddings are price insensitive and let a small product earn a large fee.
Selling in person at markets can be a customer-discovery and lead engine for higher-ticket services.
Showing the making process in short videos works well; consistency matters more than any single trick.

quote.text: consistency is like the main thing.
quote.speaker: Sariah

lessons.lesson: Selling the means to do the business (kits, supplies, courses) creates additional revenue lines beyond the product itself.
Support and warranty beat price for customers who could buy from overseas.
Simplify pricing to reduce friction and make logistics easier to estimate.
Sharing how you do it may expand the market and make you the authority rather than creating fatal competition.
Cut labor with software: removing manual photo handling lets one person do the job and raises margin.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific numbers (revenue, margins, pricing, timeline), but figures are self-reported and unverified; profit margin claims vary and the host's margin maths are hypothetical.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sariah sells machine kits, supplies and courses; Koerner promotes Go High Level and his Plans of Granger community.
